idiom_name: discriminated union command type + exhaustive switch (or handler map)
implementation_notes: A discriminated union - each command carrying a literal type field - is the canonical TypeScript command message: narrowing on the discriminant gives the handler the exact payload type, and a never-typed default branch (or a mapped handler record) turns a missing handler into a compile error, replacing the command class hierarchy and its runtime casting. The union is also the JSON shape, so the type and the wire form stay aligned, and transport is a plain JSON channel (broker client, WebSocket, worker thread) with no framework required; NestJS-style frameworks apply the same idea at a larger grain with @MessagePattern/@EventPattern pattern keys. Classes are needed only when a command must be introspected with instanceof or carry behavior at runtime.
pitfalls: Types are erased at runtime: nothing guarantees that an incoming JSON payload matches the union, so the boundary must validate (schema or a narrowing guard) before dispatch.
Widening the discriminant from literal types to string silently disables narrowing and the exhaustiveness check, and the missing-handler bug returns at runtime.
The never-check only fires inside the switch; a Record keyed by the discriminant loses exhaustiveness if the union is later opened (a string fallback key reintroduces silent no-ops).
